questions.solution_text:
$x^{2}-6x+11$
$=x^{2}-6x+3^{2}-3^{2}+11$
$=(x-3)^{2}+2$
The leftover constant $+2$ is positive, so it is a sum, not a difference, of squares. It cannot be factorised over the real numbers.
